I should’ve read the reviews before we sent our Cavapoo. I’m not giving them a one star because we are partly responsible. My husband booked a grooming, which he never does, I normally do it myself and the main concern was to get her haircut but the service he booked did not include it and include some anti-shedding work which these breeds don’t shed. So I’m very disappointed that we paid over $70 and all they basically did was bathe her. I would have expected some guidance or advise as to whether that was the right service for her, which by the way took three hours  I will definitely go back to Petco, which I shouldn’t have left in the first place

****EDIT****
I tried their grooming a second time to give them the benefit of the doubt. I stayed away from Anastasia and got Daniella. I saw she applied a $10 “handling fee” and asked why. She said my dog was giving her a hard time trimming his legs and face. I said “I told you about his legs being sensitive ahead of time.” Then she raised her voice and rudely said “well that’s the fee I added to your account because he was being difficult.” No apologies. Nothing. Then walked away. Unacceptable.

Not only that, when I was booking this grooming, I saw that Anastasia had changed my dog’s breed from Shih Tzu to Shihpoo without my consent or even my knowledge. She had no right to be making any changes to MY personal Petsmart account. And I don’t think that’s legal!

Their grooming department has officially lost my business. Do not take your fur babies here to get groomed. The only redeemer they have was how the manager handled my complaint when I talked to him, and the cashier who was very friendly and upbeat.

Looked at previous reviews for this store. And sad to say, I had a similar negative experience that reviewer, “L V” had with their Corgi. Anastasia was my dog’s groomer, and she also kept saying my dog isn’t a Shih Tzu because “he’s too big” and said they will have to up the price to another breed. That made ZERO SENSE. What do you mean change the price to another breed?? I told her well that’s what he is. I asked her is it the same price if they considered my dog a Lhasa Apso? She said she wasn’t sure. They were lucky I was in a hurry and I decided to keep his appointment. Because I didn’t get a good vibe from her at all. Thankfully, my dog came out decent. But during my conversation with her, I said to be careful because he has a mole on his front leg. Her response was basically saying well with the cut I wanted, it was most likely going to graze the mole. AKA “I’m not gonna be careful and if it happens, it happens.” I stopped going to Petsmart after previous negative experiences years ago. I thought after some time, they’d have it together by now. Looks like they don’t. The manager needs to look into Anastasia. Looks like she’s trying to scam people out of their money. And she CLEARLY is not familiar with dog breeds lol. I later looked up the typical size of Shih Tzus and online it says 9-16 pounds. My dog weighs 14 pounds. Anastasia doesn’t know what she’s doing and scammed me out of what was supposed to be a $61 groom.

*** Update ***
Its been a year or so since my review below and we went back in the store just to look at their fish and were absolutely disgusted with the state of the aquariums. There was a pile of dead/dying goldfish in one tank and the water was very cloudy. All the other tanks had filthy gravel and a ton of algae buildup. Don't buy from PetSmart.

Every time we get fish from there they always have ich. Every. Single. Time. I always think "That was a bad batch. This time will surely be different." But it never is. Don't buy fish from here unless you are content with wasting money on fish that will die in less than a month, and infect your other fish, potentially killing off your entire tank.

What an incredibly poorly managed adoption process with unprofessional staff. I visited yesterday around 6:00 PM to adopt a kitten. My family and I found one we really liked, but the identification system was a mess. There were three kittens that looked nearly identical, yet only one had a collar. Even the employees were confused, asking, “Who took off their collars?!” The only way to confirm which kitten we wanted was for them to check the gender manually.

The staff then told us they couldn’t process kitten adoptions within one hour of closing, which we understood. They took our information, assured us the kitten would be held for us at 10:00 AM the next morning, and made it seem like the adoption was essentially “reserved.” I appreciated that a lot.

When I arrived the next morning at 9:45 AM and explained the situation, the two workers immediately said, “We don’t do reservations.” I repeated exactly what we were told the night before. The employee who “helped” us struggled to even locate the kitten again because the collars were still missing. After he finally found the male kitten, he began going over the paperwork and information but noticeably skipped over whether the kitten had received its rabies vaccine.

I specifically told him I would not sign anything until he confirmed the rabies vaccine status. He agreed, took the paperwork away, and said he would check. Five minutes later, he returned with vague, confusing answers like, “I’m sure it has it, don’t worry,” and “the lady said it should, but I’m trying to make sure.” That was not good enough, so I told him I’d only fill out the basic information and wait to sign anything official until he had an actual confirmation.

While I was filling it out, he asked, “So what method of payment will you be using?” I reminded him he still hadn’t confirmed anything. That’s when his already rude, monotone attitude turned worse. He said, “I’m not going to do this with you. I’m not going over terms and conditions if it’s going to be a waste of time.” I was shocked. He rolled his eyes, had a dismissive tone, and clearly didn’t want to help.

He finally called the woman in charge of the adoptions. When I spoke with her, she had the same monotone, unhelpful demeanor and simply stated the kitten had not received its rabies vaccine. That’s all I wanted to know in the first place — an actual answer. The employee even muttered, “That’s not what she told me,” which only made the situation more concerning.

Despite all of this, I thanked him and left.

This entire experience felt chaotic, unorganized, and unprofessional. After reading some of the other reviews, I now understand why so many people described this location as suspicious or careless. If you plan to adopt from PetSmart, be aware that they may not provide accurate information and the process may be handled very poorly.

I would like to leave a one-star review for this PetSmart location La Cantera in San Antonio Tx. Yesterday, we arrived at 7:50 p.m. with the intention of adopting a cat named Zeus, an 8-week-old Russian Blue who was available at the time. The manager informed me that I had to return the next day, as adoptions were only processed until 8:00 p.m.

Trusting his word, I returned promptly at 9:00 a.m. the next morning to begin the adoption process. To my surprise, I was told that someone else had already started the adoption for Zeus. This happened despite the manager assuring me that the first person to arrive would have priority for the adoption.

Frankly, I find the situation very suspicious. We had already spoken with the staff, I followed all instructions, and I was the first to arrive the next day. The only response I received was an apology, which I do not consider sufficient. We have been looking to adopt for quite some time and had a particular interest in this cat. The way this situation was handled is very disappointing and raises serious concerns about the transparency of the adoption process at this store
